railDataReconnaissance.cityLimits: Scalar rail. kind=value carries a plain city-name string in `value` (e.g. 'Bastrop', 'Austin' -- 611,116 value rows program-wide across the top-10 city names alone) with source='landing_parcel_jurisdiction', no companion rows. kind=absent-verified (370,289 rows) is a REAL determination (verified unincorporated), not a data gap -- structured basis. No not-applicable or unaccounted rows observed in the live sample for this rail. CityLimitsFactWire (legacy shape) has NO refused/absent discriminator at all (status: incorporated|unincorporated|unmeasured) -- every parcel_record refusal (unaccounted, malformed-cell, no-such-parcel-or-rail, store-not-configured) must collapse to status='unmeasured' in the adapter; this is a real, lossy but honest simplification (unmeasured already means 'no usable determination' in the legacy type), not a fabrication.
railDataReconnaissance.wells / specialDistricts: Companion-row rails. Real value examples pulled live: wells companion payload = {api, isOrphan, wellStatus, gisWellNumber} (matches WellFactWell's needed fields); specialDistricts companion payload = {districtId, districtName, districtType} (matches SpecialDistrictFactPresent's fields exactly). Both can carry rowCount>1 (multiple companion rows per parcel) -- confirmed live (48021:103414, specialDistricts rowCount=2). absent-verified basis is a structured zone-major-sweep object identical in shape to the flood/other rails' basis convention.
